My name is not important, but I am a man of 45 years here in Tabora. This small plot of mine, about a third of a hectare, I will plant as I always do. I have no money to buy the chemical fertilizers from town, and the rains here are what they are — I cannot bring water to the field, so I must trust God and the sky. I will put some manure from my cattle on the soil because that is what my father taught me, and I will save seeds from last season like I always do. My wife and children will help me, and if the weeding becomes too much when the rains come strong, I may call a neighbor or two for a few days and pay them with food or a little money.
